subject.title: [Feature]: Per-binding and per-agent permissionMode for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add declarative per-binding and per-agent ACP permission defaults, and should that contract be `permissionMode`, `permissionProfile`, or a narrower ACP capability/policy model?
rationale: The request changes automatic write/exec approval boundaries and public config precedence, so automation should not pick the security model or migration/audit behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design scoped permissionProfile contract
options.body: Add a reviewed config contract that maps binding and agent defaults into ACP runtime permission profiles while keeping conservative fallback behavior and audit visibility.

options.title: Keep session-only tuning
options.body: Do not add static config yet; keep `/acp permissions` as the explicit operator action for per-session exceptions and close or narrow this issue after stating that policy.

options.title: Broaden to ACP policy RFC
options.body: Fold this into a larger ACP permission/capability design with nonInteractivePermissions, per-tool policy, and per-channel spawn policy rather than landing one field now.

recommendation.title: Design scoped permissionProfile contract
recommendation.body: Add a reviewed config contract that maps binding and agent defaults into ACP runtime permission profiles while keeping conservative fallback behavior and audit visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The requested precedence extends the ACP binding/default surface introduced in the persistent binding work.
